newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi sees economic upturn end-1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi sees economic upturn end-1996.

text.p: Italian Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Friday that Italy was not in recession and he expected to see an economic upturn at the end of the year.
He said in an interview with Italian state television that he also expected inflation to be under three percent at the end of 1996.

"We are not in recession. We are in a situation of Italian economic slow-down, like the majority of European economies," Ciampi said. "There are conditions to believe that this slow-down phase will be followed by an upturn."
Asked when that would happen, Ciampi said: "I am moderately confident that around the end of the year these indications of an upturn will begin to be visible."

Asked to confirm that he thought inflation would be under three percent by then, the minister added: "I have always spoken of three percent inflation. It's probable that it will be somewhat under three percent. I fully confirm that."
Forecasts based on preliminary consumer price index data from 10 Italian cities point to August inflation rising 3.3-3.4 percent year-on-year from 3.6 percent in July.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government must present the 1997 budget to parliament in September and Prodi said it aims to cut 32.4 trillion lire off next year's deficit.

Ciampi said Italians should not expect "unacceptable sacrifices", but should be aware that "the mesures we are proposing are measures that seek to give the country the credibility necessary to obtain...a fall in interest rates."
The Bank of Italy cut the discount rate by 0.75 point to 8.25 percent last month after maintaining tight monetary policy for more than a year.
